purpose: In-text citation markers expected to be detected by the Phase 2 citation parser. Each entry pins the marker text, the source span, and the expected resolution status against demo_bibliography.json.

expected_citations.rationale: Author-year parenthetical citation in the CER pivotal study sentence. Should resolve to bibliography/source-study.pdf via author normalization ('Smith J. et al.' -> 'Smith').
expected_citations.notes: Citation parser must tolerate the comma between author and year, and the 'et al.,' variant.

expected_citations.rationale: Bracketed numeric citation in the benefit-risk conclusion. There is no numbered references list in CER.docx, and no [1] target appears in bibliography/. This is the planted unresolved-citation case.
expected_citations.notes: Drives GOLD-FINDING-002. Conservative language: 'unresolved citation marker', not 'broken reference' or 'citation error'. The marker may or may not refer to Smith 2023; this is unknowable from the visible content and must remain unresolved.

expected_citations.rationale: Author-year citation in the Appendix A table 'Source' column. Same target as GOLD-CITE-001 but with stripped formatting (no parentheses, no 'et al.').
expected_citations.notes: Useful for testing citation normalization across formatting variants.

expected_citations.rationale: Second appearance of the table-cell citation form (adverse event rate row). Same target as GOLD-CITE-003.
expected_citations.notes: Multi-mention deduplication target: the same source should resolve consistently across all four mentions.

uncertainty_notes: Citation [1] in the benefit-risk conclusion is INTENTIONALLY annotated as source_unresolved rather than 'resolves to Smith 2023'. The visible content gives no deterministic mapping from [1] to any specific bibliography entry. Forcing a resolution would violate no-confident-verdict-without-evidence.
